# Parity fixtures

Reference data for the parity tests in [`crates/parity`](../../crates/parity).
Everything here, except the two vocadito recordings, is generated by the scripts
in [`reference/`](../../reference), which run the official Python
[Basic Pitch](https://github.com/spotify/basic-pitch) with its ONNX model on the
CPU.

These files are only used by the tests. They are not part of the published crates.

## Provenance and licenses

### Audio inputs (`audio/`)

| File | Format | Duration | Origin | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `synth.wav` | 44.1 kHz, mono, PCM 24 | 7.5 s | Generated by `reference/make_synth.py` | Apache-2.0, like this repository |
| `pluck.wav` | 48 kHz, stereo, PCM 24 | 10.0 s | Generated by `reference/make_synth.py` | Apache-2.0, like this repository |
| `silence.wav` | 44.1 kHz, mono, PCM 16 | 3.0 s | Generated by `reference/make_synth.py` | Apache-2.0, like this repository |
| `short.wav` | 22.05 kHz, mono, PCM 16 | 0.6 s | Generated by `reference/make_synth.py` | Apache-2.0, like this repository |
| `vocadito_10.wav` | 44.1 kHz, mono, PCM 16 | 9.1 s | vocadito dataset, via spotify/basic-pitch | CC BY 4.0 |
| `vocadito_14.wav` | 44.1 kHz, mono, PCM 16 | 12.2 s | vocadito dataset, via spotify/basic-pitch | CC BY 4.0 |

What each synthetic file exercises:

- `synth.wav`: a sine A3, a band-limited sawtooth C4, a C major triad, an E3 to
  G3 glide and a short sawtooth A4. Clean pitches, a chord and a continuous bend.
- `pluck.wav`: decaying harmonic tones shaped like guitar notes: isolated notes,
  a whole-tone bend, a vibrato, a fast run, a long held note and a power chord,
  over a light noise floor. Stereo with a slightly different right channel, so
  the downmix matters, and 48 kHz, so the resampler matters.
- `silence.wav`: digital silence. Covers the NaN path of `get_infered_onsets`
  (a division by a zero maximum) and the empty output.
- `short.wav`: shorter than one model window, already at 22 050 Hz. Covers the
  single, zero-padded window and the no-resampling path.

The synthetic files are deterministic: `make_synth.py` writes the same bytes on
every run.

**vocadito attribution.** `vocadito_10.wav` and `vocadito_14.wav` are excerpts of
*vocadito: A dataset of solo vocals with f0, note, and lyric annotations*, by
Rachel Bittner, Katherine Pasalo, Juan José Bosch, Gabriel Meseguer-Brocal and
David Rubinstein (2021), [doi:10.5281/zenodo.5578807](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5578807),
licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
They are copied unmodified from `tests/resources/` of
[spotify/basic-pitch](https://github.com/spotify/basic-pitch/tree/v0.4.0/tests/resources)
v0.4.0 (identical git blobs: `147817eb` and `ee55d884`). The technical report is
[arXiv:2110.05580](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05580).

### Reference outputs

Generated by `reference/generate_fixtures.py` from the audio above, with:

- `v0.4.0`: basic-pitch 0.4.0 from PyPI (project in `reference/`),
- `main`: spotify/basic-pitch at commit `fa5997a` (project in `reference/main/`),

both with onnxruntime 1.31.0 on the CPU, numpy 2.4.6, librosa 0.11.0
(`soxr_hq` resampling), pretty-midi 0.2.11.post0 and mido 1.3.3, on Python 3.11.
The model is `nmp.onnx`, SHA-256
`2c3c1d144bfa61ad236e92e169c13535c880469a12a047d4e73451f2c059a0ec`, the same
file as `crates/basic-pitch-rs/model/nmp.onnx`. The exact versions and the
platform of the last run are recorded in `meta-v0.4.0.json` and `meta-main.json`.

These outputs are derived from the audio inputs and keep their licenses: the
outputs of the vocadito cases are under CC BY 4.0, with the attribution above.

## Layout

```
audio/<case>.wav                 audio inputs
<case>/audio_22050.npy           audio after loading
<case>/model_input.npy           model windows (short and synth only)
<case>/raw_{note,onset,contour}.npy
<case>/v0.4.0/{note,onset,contour}.npy
<case>/v0.4.0/times.npy
<case>/v0.4.0/<config>.json      notes for one parameter set
<case>/v0.4.0/<config>.mid       MIDI file written by pretty_midi
<case>/main/times.npy
<case>/main/<config>.json
<case>/main/<config>.mid
meta-v0.4.0.json                 run metadata, per-case summary
meta-main.json
```

Cases: `synth`, `pluck`, `silence`, `short`, `vocadito_10`, `vocadito_14`.

| Case | Samples at 22 050 Hz | Windows | Frames (v0.4.0) | Frames (main) | Notes (default) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `pluck` | 220 500 | 7 | 860 | 865 | 18 |
| `short` | 13 230 | 1 | 51 | 51 | 1 |
| `silence` | 66 150 | 2 | 258 | 259 | 0 |
| `synth` | 165 375 | 5 | 645 | 649 | 9 |
| `vocadito_10` | 200 607 | 6 | 782 | 787 | 28 |
| `vocadito_14` | 268 962 | 8 | 1 049 | 1 056 | 26 |

The frame counts show the one difference between the two variants: v0.4.0 trims
the output to `floor(n_samples * 86 / 22050)` frames and drops the end of the
file, main trims to `int(n_samples / 36164 * 142)`.

## File formats

All `.npy` files are little-endian NumPy arrays (format version 1.0).

| File | dtype | Shape | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `audio_22050.npy` | f32 | `(n,)` | `librosa.load(path, sr=22050, mono=True)` |
| `model_input.npy` | f32 | `(n_windows, 43844)` | Windows exactly as fed to the model: 3840 zeros of padding in front, windows of 43 844 samples every 36 164, the last one zero-filled |
| `raw_<out>.npy` | f32 | `(n_windows, 172, bins)` | Raw model outputs, `bins` = 88 for `note` and `onset`, 264 for `contour` |
| `v0.4.0/<out>.npy` | f32 | `(n_frames, bins)` | After `unwrap_output` (15 overlapping frames removed on each side, then trimmed) |
| `<variant>/times.npy` | f64 | `(n_frames,)` | `model_frames_to_time(n_frames)` |

The unwrapped arrays of `main` are not stored: they are the same as v0.4.0 with
a few more frames at the end, and the `main` notes check them.

Each `<config>.json` holds:

| Key | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `params` | The post-processing parameters, plus `min_note_len_frames` |
| `polyphonic_events` | Output of `output_to_notes_polyphonic`, in Python's order: `[start_frame, end_frame, pitch, amplitude]` |
| `frame_events` | After `get_pitch_bends`: `[start_frame, end_frame, pitch, amplitude, bends]`, `bends` is `null` without pitch bends |
| `events` | Output of `model_output_to_notes`: `[start_s, end_s, pitch, amplitude, bends]` |
| `midi` | The `.mid` file parsed by mido: `type`, `ticks_per_beat`, and per track a list of `[absolute_tick, message]`, where `message` is mido's dict without `time` |

Events are not sorted: Python's order is part of the contract. MIDI is compared
at the level of parsed messages, not bytes.

Parameter sets (`<config>`), as overrides of the defaults of `predict()`:

| Config | Overrides |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | none: `onset_thresh=0.5`, `frame_thresh=0.3`, `min_note_len_ms=127.70`, `infer_onsets=True`, no frequency limits, pitch bends on, `multiple_pitch_bends=False`, `melodia_trick=True`, `midi_tempo=120` |
| `thresholds` | `onset_thresh=0.3`, `frame_thresh=0.2`, `min_note_len_ms=58` |
| `freq_range` | `min_freq=80`, `max_freq=1000` |
| `multiple_bends` | `multiple_pitch_bends=True` |
| `no_melodia` | `melodia_trick=False` |
| `no_infer_onsets` | `infer_onsets=False` |
| `no_bends` | `include_pitch_bends=False` |
| `tempo_90` | `midi_tempo=90` |

### Adversarial post-processing cases (`adversarial/`)

Generated by `reference/generate_adversarial.py` with basic-pitch 0.4.0, without
the model: each `<case>.json` holds synthetic posteriorgrams and, for several
parameter sets, what `note_creation.py` returns or raises. The cases reach what the
recordings above do not: thresholds at 0 and 1, plateaus where numpy's first-index
`argmax` decides, frequency bounds that become negative numpy indices, a note of
9000 frames (longer than numpy's 8192-element reduction buffer), the lowest and
highest keys and contour bins, 22 overlapping pitches with `multiple_pitch_bends`,
tempos from 3 to 100 000 BPM, `get_pitch_bends` tolerances from 0 to 1000 bins,
NaN activations, and amplitudes outside `[0, 1]`, which `pretty_midi` refuses to
write.

| Key | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `n_frames` | Number of frames |
| `note`, `onset`, `contour` | `{"fill": value, "entries": [[frame, bin, value], ...]}`: every cell is `fill` except the listed ones, all float32 |
| `runs` | One object per parameter set: `name`, `params` (as above), `polyphonic` (output of `output_to_notes_polyphonic`), then `events` and `midi`, or `error` when `model_output_to_notes` raises; `midi` is `{"error": ...}` when `pretty_midi` cannot write the file |
| `bend_tolerances` | Optional: `get_pitch_bends` with other `n_bins_tolerance` values, on the notes of the first run |

Floats that JSON cannot hold are written as the strings `"NaN"`, `"Infinity"` and
`"-Infinity"`.

## Regenerating

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). From the repository root:

```sh
cd reference
uv run --locked python -I make_synth.py ../tests/fixtures/audio
uv run --locked python -I generate_fixtures.py ../tests/fixtures ../tests/fixtures/audio/*.wav
uv run --locked python -I generate_adversarial.py ../tests/fixtures/adversarial
cd main
uv run --locked python -I ../generate_fixtures.py ../../tests/fixtures ../../tests/fixtures/audio/*.wav --variant-only
```

The vocadito files are not regenerated; copy them from spotify/basic-pitch if
they are missing. On the same platform, a run on an unchanged reference gives
byte-identical files (checked on macOS arm64). The model outputs can differ in
the last bits on another CPU architecture, and `meta-*.json` records the
platform, so commit regenerated fixtures only when the reference itself changes.
